input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It’s either not working at all or it’s very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I don’t have Wi-Fi where I am, so I rely on my phone’s internet. Can you help me get this fixed, please?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.
I tried to run the speed test, but it says there’s no connection at all. What should I do now?
It looks like Airplane Mode is turned on. Should I turn it off now? Will that help my internet work again?

Okay, I’ve turned Airplane Mode off. Now I see some signal bars and a 5G icon, but there’s also something that says “Data Disabled.” What should I do next? Should I try the speed test now, or do I need to turn something else on first?
I turned on mobile data, and now I see the “Data Enabled” icon in the status bar. But when I tried the speed test again, it still says “no connection.” What should I do now?
I checked, and my SIM card is showing as active and working. What should I try next?

I checked the APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not sure if that’s right, but that’s what it shows. What should I do now?

I reset the APN settings and rebooted my phone like you said, but the speed test still says “no connection.” I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working? Is there anything else we can try? I really need excellent internet speed.

Oh, I definitely don’t want to change my plan—I just want to add more data for now. Please go ahead and add 2GB for me. Will this make my internet excellent again? I really need it to be fast, not just working.

I rebooted my phone after adding the 2GB of data, but the speed test still says “no connection.” This is really worrying me—why isn’t it working yet? I need excellent internet speed, not just any connection. What else can we try?

Right now, I see excellent signal bars, the 5G icon, and “Data Enabled” in the status bar. There’s also something called “Data Saver” showing. I don’t see any error messages or anything else unusual. Should I turn off this Data Saver thing? Will that help my internet speed?

I turned off Data Saver mode, but the speed test still says “no connection.” The status bar still shows excellent signal, 5G, and Data Enabled. I’m really getting worried—why isn’t anything working? I just want excellent internet speed on my phone. What else can we try?

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can begin troubleshooting your mobile data problem.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

I tried to run the speed test, but it says there’s no connection at all. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your speed test shows “no connection,” let’s check a few things on your phone to diagnose the issue:

1. Please check if Airplane Mode is turned ON. If it is, turn it OFF.
2. Make sure your SIM card is properly inserted and not showing any errors.
3. Confirm that mobile data is enabled in your phone’s settings.

Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see an Airplane Mode icon,
- If there are any signal bars,
- If you see a mobile data icon (like 4G, LTE, 5G, etc.), or if it says “No Service.”

This information will help me guide you through the next steps.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
It looks like Airplane Mode is turned on. Should I turn it off now? Will that help my internet work again?

Yes, please turn Airplane Mode OFF. When Airplane Mode is on, it disables all wireless connections, including your mobile data and cellular service. Turning it off should restore your phone’s ability to connect to the internet.

After you turn Airplane Mode off, wait a few moments and check if your mobile data connection returns. If possible, try running the speed test again and let me know the result. If you still have issues, please let me know what icons you see in your status bar after turning Airplane Mode off.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I’ve turned Airplane Mode off. Now I see some signal bars and a 5G icon, but there’s also something that says “Data Disabled.” What should I do next? Should I try the speed test now, or do I need to turn something else on first?

Since you see “Data Disabled,” your mobile data is currently turned off. Please enable mobile data in your phone’s settings first. Once mobile data is turned on, you should see the “Data Enabled” icon in your status bar.

After enabling mobile data, try running the speed test again and let me know the result. If you need help finding the mobile data setting on your phone, let me know your device type (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you through the steps.

Mobile Data is now ON.

I turned on mobile data, and now I see the “Data Enabled” icon in the status bar. But when I tried the speed test again, it still says “no connection.” What should I do now?

Thank you for the update. Since mobile data is enabled but you still have no connection, let’s check your SIM card status next. Please check your SIM card status in your phone’s settings and let me know if it shows as “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked.” 

If you need instructions on how to check your SIM card status, let me know your device type (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you through the steps.
Your SIM card is active and working.
I checked, and my SIM card is showing as active and working. What should I try next?

Since your SIM card is active and working, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent your mobile data from working.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if anything looks incorrect or if you see a missing or blank field, especially for the APN name or MMSC URL. If you’re unsure how to check this, let me know your device type (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you through the process.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked the APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not sure if that’s right, but that’s what it shows. What should I do now?

Thank you for providing your APN details. Since your APN name and MMSC URL are filled in, let’s try resetting your APN settings to the default values. This can often resolve hidden configuration issues.

Please reset your APN settings to default on your phone. After resetting, you must reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Once you’ve done both steps (reset APN settings and reboot your phone), try running the speed test again and let me know if your mobile data is working. If you need instructions for resetting APN settings or rebooting your device, let me know your device type.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
